# First, define a function that checks if a package is installed. 
# If not, it installs it. Then it loads it.
package_loader <- function(pkg) {
  if (!require(pkg, character.only = TRUE)) {
    message(paste("Installing missing package:", pkg))
    install.packages(pkg, dependencies = TRUE)
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}

# Load here package to be able to locate subsequent files
package_loader("here")

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(zoo)
library(neverhpfilter)
library(xts)

# 1. Aggregate Quarterly (Keep ALL rows)
master_q_df <- master_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(employment)) %>%
  mutate(quarter = as.yearqtr(date)) %>%
  group_by(quarter) %>%
  summarise(
    unemployment      = mean(unemployment, na.rm = TRUE),
    employment        = mean(employment, na.rm = TRUE),
    gdp               = mean(gdp, na.rm = TRUE),
    unemp_5y_forecast = mean(`5y_unemp_forecast`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

master_q_df <- master_q_df %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Calculate the denominator (Labor Force)
    labor_force = employment + unemployment,
    
    # 2. Calculate the Rate in Percentage Points (e.g., 3.5)
    u_rate = (unemployment / labor_force) * 100
  )

# Now check the values
summary(master_q_df$u_rate)

# 1. Calculate Log GDP
master_q_df$log_gdp <- log(master_q_df$gdp)

# 2. Fill NAs for the filter
log_gdp_filled <- na.approx(master_q_df$log_gdp, na.rm = FALSE)
gdp_xts <- xts(log_gdp_filled, order.by = master_q_df$quarter)

# 3. Run Hamilton Filter on LOGS
hamilton_output <- yth_filter(gdp_xts, h = 8, p = 4)

# 4. Extract the Log-Gap
gdp_gap_df <- data.frame(
  quarter = index(hamilton_output),
  # This is now in decimal percentage (e.g., -0.015)
  gdp_gap = as.numeric(hamilton_output$y.cycle) 
)

# 5. Join and Prepare for Model
master_final_q <- master_q_df %>%
  inner_join(gdp_gap_df, by = "quarter") %>%
  mutate(
    # Ensure Unemployment is also in decimals for consistency
    u_rate_dec = u_rate / 100,
    spf_dec    = unemp_5y_forecast / 100
  )





summary(master_final_q$gdp_gap)
```

```{r}
# 1. Create Lagged Matrix for Okun's Law
X_reg <- cbind(
  y0 = master_final_q$gdp_gap,
  y1 = dplyr::lag(master_final_q$gdp_gap, 1),
  y2 = dplyr::lag(master_final_q$gdp_gap, 2)
)

# 2. Extract Observations (Unemployment and SPF)
# SPF will have NAs before 2015, which is correct!
Y_obs <- as.matrix(master_final_q[, c("u_rate_dec", "spf_dec")])

# 3. Final Trimming: Remove the first 2 rows where lags (y1, y2) are NA
keep_idx <- complete.cases(X_reg)

X_reg_final <- X_reg[keep_idx, ]

# Check the range: it should now be roughly between -0.2 and 0.2
summary(X_reg_final[,1])

Y_obs_final <- Y_obs[keep_idx, ]

message("Ready to run! Observations: ", nrow(Y_obs_final))
```

cor(Y_obs_final[,1], X_reg_final[,1], use = "complete.obs")

```{r}
library(dlm)
# 1. DATA PREP: Ensure the first row of SPF isn't the problem
# If SPF is NA at the very start, we can't 'anchor' its initial variance easily.
# We set the first SPF value to the first Unemployment value just for the m0/C0 initialization.
Y_final_fixed <- Y_obs_final
if(is.na(Y_final_fixed[1, 2])) {
  Y_final_fixed[1, 2] <- Y_final_fixed[1, 1] 
}

# 2. OBJECTIVE FUNCTION: Stability Improvements
objective_fn_ultimate <- function(parm, Y, X) {
  # parm: [log_s_trend, log_s_u, log_s_spf, beta0, beta1, beta2]
  
  s_trend <- exp(parm[1])
  s_u     <- exp(parm[2])
  s_spf   <- exp(parm[3])
  betas   <- parm[4:6]
  
  # 1. Calculate the Okun cycle
  # Ensure X has no NAs: X <- na.approx(X) if necessary
  cycle <- as.matrix(X) %*% as.matrix(betas)
  
  # 2. Adjust Unemployment
  Y_adj <- Y
  Y_adj[, 1] <- Y_adj[, 1] - cycle
  
  # 3. Build the Model with 'Inf' safety
  # We use a slightly larger C0 so the filter can find the trend 
  # even if the first few observations are noisy.
  mod <- dlm(
    FF = matrix(c(1, 1), nrow = 2),
    V  = diag(c(s_u, s_spf)) + diag(1e-7, 2), 
    GG = matrix(1),
    W  = matrix(s_trend),
    m0 = mean(Y[, 1], na.rm = TRUE),
    C0 = matrix(0.01) 
  )
  
  # 4. Compute Likelihood with Error Catching
  # If dlmLL fails, we return a large number
  out <- tryCatch({
    val <- dlmLL(Y_adj, mod)
    if(is.na(val) || !is.finite(val)) 1e10 else val
  }, error = function(e) 1e10)
  
  return(out)
}

# 3. TEST RUN
init_guess <- c(-8, -6, -6, -0.4, -0.1, -0.05)
test_run <- objective_fn_ultimate(init_guess, Y_final_fixed, X_reg_final)
print(paste("Likelihood at start:", test_run))
```

```{r}
# =========================
# 0. LIBRARIES
# =========================
library(dplyr)
library(zoo)
library(neverhpfilter)
library(xts)
library(dlm)

# =========================
# 1. QUARTERLY AGGREGATION
# =========================
master_q_df <- master_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(employment)) %>%
  mutate(quarter = as.yearqtr(date)) %>%
  group_by(quarter) %>%
  summarise(
    unemployment      = mean(unemployment, na.rm = TRUE),
    employment        = mean(employment, na.rm = TRUE),
    gdp               = mean(gdp, na.rm = TRUE),
    unemp_5y_forecast = mean(`5y_unemp_forecast`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    labor_force = employment + unemployment,
    u_rate      = (unemployment / labor_force) * 100
  )

# =========================
# 2. GDP GAP (HAMILTON FILTER)
# =========================
master_q_df$log_gdp <- log(master_q_df$gdp)

# Interpolate ONLY if necessary (kept minimal)
log_gdp_filled <- na.approx(master_q_df$log_gdp, na.rm = FALSE)

gdp_xts <- xts(log_gdp_filled, order.by = master_q_df$quarter)

hamilton_output <- yth_filter(gdp_xts, h = 8, p = 4)

gdp_gap_df <- data.frame(
  quarter = index(hamilton_output),
  gdp_gap = as.numeric(hamilton_output$y.cycle)  # log deviation
)

# =========================
# 3. MERGE + TRANSFORM
# =========================
master_final_q <- master_q_df %>%
  inner_join(gdp_gap_df, by = "quarter") %>%
  mutate(
    u_rate_dec = u_rate / 100,
    spf_dec    = unemp_5y_forecast / 100
  )

# =========================
# 4. BUILD REGRESSION MATRIX (OKUN)
# =========================
X_reg <- cbind(
  y0 = master_final_q$gdp_gap,
  y1 = dplyr::lag(master_final_q$gdp_gap, 1),
  y2 = dplyr::lag(master_final_q$gdp_gap, 2)
)

Y_obs <- as.matrix(master_final_q[, c("u_rate_dec", "spf_dec")])

# =========================
# 5. TRIMMING (CRITICAL FIX)
# =========================
# Keep rows where:
# - X is complete (lags valid)
# - unemployment is observed
keep_idx <- complete.cases(X_reg) & !is.na(Y_obs[,1])

X_reg_final <- X_reg[keep_idx, ]
Y_obs_final <- Y_obs[keep_idx, ]

message("Observations after trimming: ", nrow(Y_obs_final))

# =========================
# 6. OBJECTIVE FUNCTION
# =========================
objective_fn <- function(parm, Y, X) {
  
  if(any(is.na(parm)) || length(parm) != 6) return(1e10)
  
  s_trend <- exp(parm[1])
  s_u     <- exp(parm[2])
  s_spf   <- exp(parm[3])
  betas   <- parm[4:6]
  
  if(length(betas) != ncol(X)) return(1e10)
  
  cycle <- as.matrix(X) %*% as.matrix(betas)
  if(any(!is.finite(cycle))) return(1e10)
  
  Y_adj <- Y
  Y_adj[,1] <- Y_adj[,1] - cycle
  
  # =========================
  # KEY FIX: HANDLE SPF BLOCKWISE
  # =========================
  
  valid_spf <- !is.na(Y_adj[,2])
  
  # Split sample
  Y1 <- Y_adj[!valid_spf, 1, drop = FALSE]      # unemployment only
  Y2 <- Y_adj[valid_spf, , drop = FALSE]        # joint system
  
  ll_total <- 0
  
  # ---- Part 1: Pre-SPF (unemployment only) ----
  if(nrow(Y1) > 5) {
    
    mod1 <- dlm(
      FF = matrix(1),
      V  = matrix(s_u + 1e-7),
      GG = matrix(1),
      W  = matrix(s_trend),
      m0 = mean(Y1, na.rm = TRUE),
      C0 = matrix(0.01)
    )
    
    ll1 <- tryCatch(dlmLL(Y1, mod1), error = function(e) NA)
    
    if(is.na(ll1) || !is.finite(ll1)) return(1e10)
    
    ll_total <- ll_total + ll1
  }
  
  # ---- Part 2: With SPF (joint system) ----
  if(nrow(Y2) > 5) {
    
    mod2 <- dlm(
      FF = matrix(c(1,1), nrow = 2),
      V  = diag(c(s_u, s_spf)) + diag(1e-7, 2),
      GG = matrix(1),
      W  = matrix(s_trend),
      m0 = mean(Y2[,1], na.rm = TRUE),
      C0 = matrix(0.01)
    )
    
    ll2 <- tryCatch(dlmLL(Y2, mod2), error = function(e) NA)
    
    if(is.na(ll2) || !is.finite(ll2)) return(1e10)
    
    ll_total <- ll_total + ll2
  }
  
  return(ll_total)
}

# =========================
# 7. INITIAL VALUES
# =========================
init_guess <- c(
  -10,   # trend variance
  -7,    # unemployment noise
  -7,    # SPF noise
  -0.4,  # Okun beta contemporaneous
  -0.1,  # lag 1
  -0.05  # lag 2
)

# =========================
# 8. SANITY CHECKS
# =========================
cat("NA in X:", any(is.na(X_reg_final)), "\n")
cat("NA in unemployment:", any(is.na(Y_obs_final[,1])), "\n")
cat("Initial likelihood:", objective_fn(init_guess, Y_obs_final, X_reg_final), "\n")

# Check Okun sign
cat("Correlation (should be negative): ",
    cor(Y_obs_final[,1], X_reg_final[,1], use = "complete.obs"), "\n")

# =========================
# 9. OPTIMIZATION (Method Fixed)
# =========================
opt <- optim(
  par     = init_guess,
  fn      = objective_fn,
  Y       = Y_obs_final,
  X       = X_reg_final,
  method  = "L-BFGS-B",  # Mandatory for bounds
  lower   = c(-20, -15, -8, -2, -1, -1), # SPF noise bound will now work
  upper   = c(-5, -2, -2, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
  control = list(maxit = 500, trace = 1)
)

# =========================
# 10. RESULTS & MODEL RECONSTRUCTION
# =========================
est_par <- opt$par
s_trend <- exp(est_par[1])
s_u     <- exp(est_par[2])
s_spf   <- exp(est_par[3])
betas   <- est_par[4:6]

# Re-calculate the cycle
final_cycle_vector <- as.matrix(X_reg_final) %*% as.matrix(betas)

# Create Adjusted Y (the part the trend must explain)
Y_adj_final <- Y_obs_final
Y_adj_final[, 1] <- Y_adj_final[, 1] - final_cycle_vector

# Define the final Bivariate Model
# We add a tiny 'nugget' for numerical stability
final_mod <- dlm(
  FF = matrix(c(1, 1), nrow = 2),
  V  = diag(c(s_u, s_spf)) + diag(1e-8, 2), 
  GG = matrix(1),
  W  = matrix(s_trend),
  m0 = mean(Y_adj_final[, 1], na.rm = TRUE),
  C0 = matrix(0.1)
)
# ==========================================
# 11. RECONSTRUCTION WITH DUAL-SOURCE NOISE
# ==========================================

# 1. Extract and regularize variances
# We use a floor of 1e-5 (log -11.5). This is small enough to be accurate 
# but large enough to prevent the "division by zero" NaN error.
s_trend_final <- max(exp(opt$par[1]), 1e-6) # Structural change variance
s_u_final     <- max(exp(opt$par[2]), 1e-5) # Noise in Unemployment
s_spf_final   <- max(exp(opt$par[3]), 1e-4) # Noise in SPF (Expert Error)

betas_final   <- opt$par[4:6]

# 2. Re-calculate Okun Cycle
final_cycle_vec <- as.matrix(X_reg_final) %*% as.matrix(betas_final)

# 3. Adjust Unemployment
Y_adj_robust <- Y_obs_final
Y_adj_robust[, 1] <- Y_adj_robust[, 1] - final_cycle_vec

# 4. Build the Bivariate Model
# C0 = 1.0 is vital here; it tells the filter to 'search' for the trend 
# rather than assuming it knows exactly where it starts.
mod_robust <- dlm(
  FF = matrix(c(1, 1), nrow = 2),
  V  = diag(c(s_u_final, s_spf_final)),
  GG = matrix(1),
  W  = matrix(s_trend_final),
  m0 = mean(Y_adj_robust[, 1], na.rm = TRUE),
  C0 = matrix(1.0) 
)

# 5. Run the Filter
filt_robust <- dlmFilter(Y_adj_robust, mod_robust)

# ==========================================
# 12. EXTRACTION (THE FINAL LINE)
# ==========================================
# Extract states (dropping m0)
trend_final <- filt_robust$m[-1, 1, drop = TRUE]

results_df <- data.frame(
  quarter       = master_final_q$quarter[keep_idx],
  actual_u_rate = Y_obs_final[, 1] * 100,
  natural_rate  = as.numeric(trend_final) * 100,
  spf_anchor    = Y_obs_final[, 2] * 100,
  okun_cycle    = as.numeric(final_cycle_vec) * 100
)

# Final Check
print("Natural Rate Values (Should be numbers now!):")
print(head(results_df$natural_rate))
```

```{r}
# =========================
# 11. FINAL MODEL (SMOOTHING)
# =========================
filtered_final <- dlmFilter(Y_adj_final, final_mod)
smoothed_final <- dlmSmooth(filtered_final)

# Check the object structure
# s is a matrix/vector of length (N+1) because it includes the initial state m0
s_vector <- smoothed_final$s

if (is.matrix(s_vector)) {
  # If it's a matrix, take all rows except the first, and the first column
  trend_values <- s_vector[-1, 1]
} else {
  # If it's a vector, just take all elements except the first
  trend_values <- s_vector[-1]
}

# =========================
# 12. OUTPUT DATAFRAME & SCALING
# =========================
results_df <- data.frame(
  quarter       = master_final_q$quarter[keep_idx],
  actual_u_rate = Y_obs_final[, 1] * 100,       # Back to % (e.g., 3.5)
  spf_forecast  = Y_obs_final[, 2] * 100,       # Back to %
  natural_rate  = as.numeric(trend_values) * 100, 
  okun_cycle    = as.numeric(final_cycle) * 100
)

# Calculate the Unemployment Gap (Cyclical Unemployment)
results_df$u_gap <- results_df$actual_u_rate - results_df$natural_rate

# VERIFY: This should finally show numbers
print("Final Check - Natural Rate Values:")
print(head(results_df$natural_rate))
```



```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Convert yearqtr to Date for perfect plotting
results_df$date_plot <- as.Date(results_df$quarter)

ggplot(results_df, aes(x = date_plot)) +
  # Actual Unemployment (the raw data)
  geom_line(aes(y = actual_u_rate, color = "Actual Unemployment"), 
            linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  # The Estimated Natural Rate (the smooth trend)
  geom_line(aes(y = natural_rate, color = "Natural Rate (Trend)"), 
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Add the SPF for comparison (it will only show up from 2015+)
  geom_point(aes(y = spf_forecast, color = "SPF 5y Forecast"), 
             size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Decomposition of Swiss Unemployment",
       subtitle = "State-Space Model: Okun's Law + SPF Expectations",
       y = "Unemployment Rate",
       x = "Year",
       color = "Series") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
